author: WP16
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on how sharp-runtime verifies itself: three test locations, per-component executables, the non-green measured gate, negative consumers, the audit data set, review findings, sanitizer results and the reproducibility seam. All counts moved by 41b918c9 (527 test files, 40/44 tested modules, 58 negative fixtures/284 sites, 343/19/2 audit statuses, ten CI configurations). None of it was on the site; it is now on the parity-and-verification deep dive.

concepts.section: Verification and Audit in sharp-runtime
concepts.text: sharp-runtime's verification combines component GoogleTest programs, integration tests, compile boundaries, positive and negative consumers, Python meta-tests, sanitizer runs and an audit record, and is not summarised as all passing.
tokens: does not summarise its state as

concepts.section: Three test locations have three jobs
concepts.text: modules/<module>/tests/ holds the primary unit tests mirroring each module: 527 C++ files at 41b918c9.

concepts.section: Three test locations have three jobs
concepts.text: tests/ holds cross-component integration tests and the i686 compile-boundary source.

concepts.section: Three test locations have three jobs
concepts.text: test/ holds Python meta-tests and CMake consumer fixtures, some of which must fail to compile.
concepts.note: Post-Phase-3 adversarial audit correction: sharp-runtime's test directory lists eleven Python meta-tests, not twelve (audit finding C10 ch58-F1).

concepts.section: Three test locations have three jobs
concepts.text: GoogleTest is a required vendored submodule; tests create one executable per component owning tests plus an integration executable, with the component name as prefix.

concepts.section: The executable boundary tests the dependency boundary
concepts.text: Each component test executable links its component, gtest_main and only declared TEST_DEPENDENCIES, so a test crossing an undeclared edge fails to link.

concepts.section: The executable boundary tests the dependency boundary
concepts.text: Source-partition validation and an empty allowlist reinforce the boundary before execution; test-only edges stay separate from production edges.

concepts.section: The executable boundary tests the dependency boundary
concepts.text: Four module directories have no component tests at 41b918c9; listing them is more informative than a global count implying uniform coverage.

concepts.section: The measured gate is not green
concepts.text: The measured gate at 41b918c9 is recorded as 17,934 tests/39 executables (2026-08-31) and five Xml.Linq failures on 2026-09-19; older figures describe other revisions.

concepts.section: The measured gate is not green
concepts.text: Executable count reconciles as components with tests plus one integration executable; meta-tests, consumer cases, probes and audit docs are not GoogleTest registrations.
tokens: must not be added to a test total

concepts.section: The measured gate is not green
concepts.text: The test-to-production line ratio signals investment, not proof; untested components and recorded failures remain visible.
concepts.note: Physical lines at 41b918c9: 187,414 test vs 191,545 production.

concepts.section: Negative consumers prove absence
concepts.text: A positive consumer asks whether the intended dependency compiles; a negative consumer asks whether a forbidden one fails.

concepts.section: Negative consumers prove absence
concepts.text: Fixtures cover forbidden Text.Json-to-Collections and XML-to-Diagnostics edges, collection setters/enumerators, generic math and cryptographic key material.

concepts.section: Negative consumers prove absence
concepts.text: Negative sites are marked SHARP_RUNTIME_NEGATIVE_SITE/NEGATIVE(id) and compiled once per site; failure at the expected site is success, so a Python checker inspects outcome and site.

concepts.section: Negative consumers prove absence
concepts.text: At 41b918c9 test/consumer holds 58 negative and 25 positive fixtures with 284 NEGATIVE markers.

concepts.section: Negative consumers prove absence
concepts.text: Top-level Python meta-tests include validate_module_boundaries_test.py, check_negative_consumer_fixtures_test.py and check_version_seam_odr_test.py.

concepts.section: Audit is a tracked data set
concepts.text: audit/ holds 1,748 *.audit.md files, close to one per tracked source file.

concepts.section: Audit is a tracked data set
concepts.text: AUDIT_FINDINGS_INDEX.md assigns stable SR-AUD ids frozen at 364; at 41b918c9: 343 remediated, 19 accepted deviations, 2 false positives, none open.

concepts.section: Audit is a tracked data set
concepts.text: Confirmed means still open for a reason, remediated means repaired with gates passed; frozen identifiers stop denominator games.

concepts.section: Audit is a tracked data set
concepts.text: Planning apparatus: 288 Markdown docs, plan.md and a tracked plan.sqlite3 (8,982,528 bytes) kept despite a matching .gitignore rule; not runtime code.

concepts.section: A completed task list triggered more skepticism
concepts.text: A fully checked-off ticket table led to fresh reviews that found defects happy-path tests had missed.

concepts.section: A completed task list triggered more skepticism
concepts.text: Floating-point Convert used static_cast truncation; it now rounds to nearest, ties to even.

concepts.section: A completed task list triggered more skepticism
concepts.text: Dictionary's non-const operator[] inserted on read; a ValueProxy now throws KeyNotFoundException on reads.

concepts.section: A completed task list triggered more skepticism
concepts.text: ConcurrentDictionary factories ran under a non-recursive mutex and self-deadlocked; the factory now runs outside the lock.

concepts.section: A completed task list triggered more skepticism
concepts.text: Mutable collections lacked fail-fast checks and MemoryStream::Write allowed a negative offset; both were repaired type by type.

concepts.section: A completed task list triggered more skepticism
concepts.text: Each repair needed a type-specific oracle, not a generic clean-up.

concepts.section: Sanitizers answer a different class of question
concepts.text: Sanitizers found races (Task::Wait, Lazy, TimeZoneInfo::Local, TimeSpan counters), an AlignedRealloc heap overflow, XML DOM leaks and a null fwrite in ZIP writing; the Channel lost wake-up came from a review.
concepts.note: Bible attributed the Channel fix to ThreadSanitizer.

concepts.section: Sanitizers answer a different class of question
concepts.text: TaskCompletionSource::TrySetResult claimed completion before copying; a throwing copy stranded all waiters until the copy failure was stored in the promise and rethrown.

concepts.section: Sanitizers answer a different class of question
concepts.text: Sanitizers do not prove .NET parity; numeric or API deviations can survive a sanitizer-clean run.

concepts.section: Reproducibility has an external seam
concepts.text: The porting rules rely on a .NET reference tree at /rv/tmp/runtime/src/libraries/ outside the repository, neither vendored nor pinned.

concepts.section: Reproducibility has an external seam
concepts.text: The environment recorded in an August 2026 handoff lacked the reference tree, Doxygen and ccache.
concepts.note: Describes the tool environment of one past handoff session, not the library; the reproducibility caveat itself is kept on the page.

concepts.section: Reproducibility has an external seam
concepts.text: A fail-fast local gate and one Ubuntu workflow run ten selective configurations, the full compatibility gate and Doxygen validation with a two-job ceiling.

concepts.section: Reproducibility has an external seam
concepts.text: Workflow presence is not proof that every revision passed and gives no Windows/macOS/Emscripten execution; native pass, cross-compile and cross execution are separate results.

concepts.section: Reproducibility has an external seam
concepts.text: The strongest verification property is stating what each layer proved and keeping failures under stable ids; CNA reports touching System:: paths should name the sibling revision and keep its failures in view.
